newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura's Sakamaki says he met racketeer Koike once.
newsitem.headline: Nomura's Sakamaki says he met racketeer Koike once.

text.p: Hideo Sakamaki, former president of Nomura Securities Co Ltd, said on Wednesday he met the "sokaiya" corporate racketeer at the centre of a loans and payoff scandal on one occasion after becoming president.

Sakamaki, who resigned his post after the scandal broke and is now a Nomura adviser, told a parliamentary committee that the meeting with Ryuichi Koike took place in 1992 at the request of a Nomura executive.
The executive asked him to meet Koike as he was a long-standing Nomura shareholder, having held a stake in the firm since 1970, Sakamaki said.
But Sakamaki said he did not know that Koike had been making stock transactions through Nomura.
Koike is under arrest on suspicion of taking illegal payoffs from Nomura.

Earlier this month, Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Council (SESC), sought legal action against Nomura by filing a criminal complaint with prosecutors against the firm, two former Nomura executives and a company official, alleging that they compensated a client linked to a racketeer for investment losses.
The complaint came after Nomura itself announced on March 6 that executives had been involved in irregular stock deals.
Since then, prosecutors have arrested two former Nomura executives and a Nomura general manager as well as Koike and his younger brother, Yoshinori Koike.
